metadata.author: pdfnative-cli samples
metadata.subject: Byte-identical output across hosts and runs: --creation-date / SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (v1.5.0, pdfnative 1.8.0)
metadata.keywords: reproducible builds, source date epoch, deterministic

blocks.text: Unencrypted pdfnative output is a pure function of its inputs plus one instant: the creation date. /Info /CreationDate, xmp:CreateDate, the {date} placeholder printed in this page's header and the trailer /ID (an MD5 over title, creation date and object count) all derive from it, and since pdfnative 1.8.0 every date is written in UTC — so pinning the instant makes the bytes identical on a laptop in Paris and a CI runner in UTC.

items: --creation-date 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z — a global flag, so a batch --manifest pipeline inherits it.
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1767225600 — the reproducible-builds.org convention (integer seconds); used when the flag is absent.
layout.creationDate in the document JSON or a --layout file — revived from an ISO string.

blocks.text: Encrypted output (the file key and AES IVs come from a CSPRNG by design — ISO 32000-1 §7.6), native ECDSA signatures (a random nonce; --pure-crypto uses RFC 6979 deterministic nonces), and anything stamped by a timestamp authority. Signing time (sign --signing-time) and metadata --mod-date are separate instants with a legal meaning of their own and are not covered by the pin.
Run samples/render/reproducible/01-double-render.sh (or .ps1): it renders this document twice under two time zones and compares the SHA-256 hashes.
